questions.questionText: Read the following: After a new flyover opened at Koyambedu, the bus travel time on a Chennai route fell from 50 to 35 minutes. Officials say the flyover is responsible. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The flyover has four lanes.
Some commuters still prefer autorickshaws on that route.
In the same period the bus company removed 30% of the stops on that route.
The flyover was built by a Chennai-based firm.
questions.explanation: A different change in the same period (fewer stops) could by itself shorten the journey, so it offers an alternative cause and weakens the claim.
questions.shortcut: Look for another factor that could produce the same effect.

questions.questionText: Read the following: In a Jaipur school, students who bring home-cooked tiffin score higher than those who eat in the canteen. The principal says home food improves scores. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Tiffin boxes are checked by the class teacher.
Canteen food is cheaper than home-cooked food.
Students who bring tiffin mostly come from families that can afford private tuition.
The school has 1,200 students.
questions.explanation: Private tuition is a rival explanation for the higher scores, so the link to home food is weakened.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A mobile phone company released an advertisement featuring a famous cricketer, and its sales rose 25% that quarter. The company's marketing head says the advertisement caused the rise. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The advertisement was shown on four TV channels.
The cricketer has endorsed other products too.
The cricket World Cup began in that quarter, and sales of all phone brands rose by about 25%.
The company's phones come in three colours.
questions.explanation: If every brand's sales rose by the same amount, the common cause (the tournament period) explains the rise and the advertisement is not needed.

questions.questionText: Read the following: At a Hyderabad hospital, heart-surgery patients who attend yoga classes recover faster. The hospital argues that yoga speeds up recovery. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The yoga classes are held in the morning.
Yoga is taught by a certified instructor.
Only patients who are already recovering well are physically able to attend the classes.
The hospital performs about 300 heart surgeries a year.
questions.explanation: This reverses the cause and effect: good recovery allows attendance, not the other way round.
questions.shortcut: Check whether the effect might actually be the cause.

questions.questionText: Read the following: Enrolment in Bihar's government schools rose by 12% over three years. The state claims that its mid-day meal scheme was responsible for the rise. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The meal scheme serves rice and dal.
The scheme is funded jointly by the Centre and the state.
The number of school-age children in Bihar rose by 14% over the same three years.
Some private schools also offer meals.
questions.explanation: If the school-age population grew faster than enrolment, the rise in enrolment is explained by demographics and does not need the scheme.

questions.questionText: Read the following: To reduce power cuts, Uttarakhand plans to build several small hydroelectric plants, assuming they will generate steady power through the year. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The plants will be built over three years.
Hydropower does not release carbon dioxide.
Most of the rivers where the plants are proposed run almost dry for five months of the year.
The state has many tourists in summer.
questions.explanation: The plan depends on year-round water; if the rivers run dry for five months, steady output is undermined.

questions.questionText: Read the following: An online coaching app says that 90% of its subscribers cleared the exam, which it says proves its quality. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The app has been downloaded by lakhs of students.
The app charges a monthly fee.
The 90% figure counts only subscribers who completed the entire course, and about 70% of subscribers drop out before the end.
Its lectures are recorded in Hindi and English.
questions.explanation: Counting only those who completed the course ignores most subscribers, so the success rate is inflated by selection.

questions.questionText: Read the following: In a pilot village, drip irrigation cut water use by 40%. The cooperative concludes it will cut water use by about 40% in all its villages. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The pilot lasted one season.
Drip systems are made of plastic tubing.
The pilot village was chosen because its water losses under flood irrigation were unusually high compared with other villages.
The cooperative has 12 villages.
questions.explanation: An atypical pilot site cannot be taken to represent other villages, so the expected saving elsewhere is likely lower.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A Kolkata sweet-shop owner says his rasgulla sales dropped because a rival shop opened nearby. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The rival shop sells many kinds of sweets.
The rival shop is on the same road.
His rasgulla sales had been falling steadily for two years before the rival shop opened.
The owner's shop opens at 8 am.
questions.explanation: If the decline began long before the rival came, the rival cannot be its cause.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A Delhi airline says that its on-time record of 92% shows how much it values passengers' time. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The airline operates 150 flights a day.
Its on-time record is published monthly.
The airline adds 30 minutes to the scheduled duration of every flight, so flights arrive 'on time' even if they are slow.
Some of its aircraft are leased.
questions.explanation: Padding the schedule makes punctuality easy to achieve without saving passengers any time, so it undermines the inference.

questions.questionText: Read the following: Vimal argues that switching to an electric bike will save him ₹4,000 a month, as he now spends ₹5,000 monthly on petrol and charging would cost only ₹1,000. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Electric bikes are quieter than petrol bikes.
Charging takes about four hours.
The electric bike requires a monthly battery lease of ₹3,500.
Petrol prices change every day.
questions.explanation: The lease cost cuts the actual saving to ₹500, so the conclusion is badly weakened.

questions.questionText: Read the following: The government claims that cashless payment at ration shops reduced corruption, since complaints about ration shops fell by 30%. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Cashless payment is done through a card.
Ration shops open at 9 am.
The complaint helpline which recorded these complaints was discontinued for part of the period.
The scheme was launched by the state food department.
questions.explanation: If the means of recording complaints was shut, fewer complaints may reflect fewer records rather than less corruption.

questions.questionText: Read the following: Since automatic doors were installed on some Mumbai local trains, deaths from falling off trains have fallen. A railway official says the doors save lives. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The doors close in about ten seconds.
Automatic doors cost several lakh rupees per coach.
The trains with automatic doors run only on air-conditioned services, where almost nobody travelled on footboards even earlier.
Mumbai local trains carry millions of passengers daily.
questions.explanation: If the risk was already negligible on those trains, the fall in deaths cannot be attributed to the doors.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A college hostel warden argues that exam stress causes students' hair fall, because hair fall complaints peak in exam months. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Students sleep less during exams.
The hostel has a gym.
Hair fall among students in this college peaks every year in the monsoon months, which also happen to be the exam months.
Complaints are made to the warden.
questions.explanation: A seasonal factor (monsoon) offers an alternative explanation for the same pattern.

questions.questionText: Read the following: Researchers found that Indian districts with more mobile phones have higher female literacy. They conclude that mobile phones raise literacy. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Mobile phone ownership has grown rapidly in India.
Literacy is measured by census surveys.
Mobile towers were installed first in districts that already had high literacy and better roads.
Some districts have very few towers.
questions.explanation: If phones arrived where literacy was already high, the cause could be the reverse or a common factor, so the claimed effect is undermined.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A tea company says that since its Assam tea has just won an international award, its exports will rise next year. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The award was announced in London.
The company was founded in 1950.
A 30% import duty on tea will take effect next month in its largest importing country.
Tea is picked mostly by hand.
questions.explanation: A new heavy duty works directly against export growth and outweighs any boost from the award.

questions.questionText: Read the following: Kerala's literacy programme succeeded through a network of community libraries and volunteers. A minister says the same programme will succeed in Rajasthan. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The programme in Kerala began in 1989.
Rajasthan is larger than Kerala.
Rajasthan has almost no community libraries and few volunteer organisations.
Rajasthan has many tourists.
questions.explanation: An analogy fails if the two cases differ in a feature on which the programme's success depended.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A school principal says smart boards raised the Class 8 mathematics average by 10 marks. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Smart boards were installed in June.
The smart boards have 75-inch screens.
Class 8 was also the only class to receive a new, highly experienced mathematics teacher that year.
The school has classes from 1 to 12.
questions.explanation: An additional change for the same class (a new experienced teacher) offers another explanation for the gain.

questions.questionText: Read the following: Autorickshaw fares in a city have been raised by 20%. An owners' association says that its members' earnings will rise by 20%. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Autorickshaws run on CNG in the city.
The fare increase was announced in January.
Higher fares will push many customers to app-based cabs, so the number of autorickshaw rides will drop.
Meters are checked every year.
questions.explanation: Earnings depend on both fare and number of rides; if rides fall, earnings need not rise by 20%.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A poll of 1,000 people found that 60% favour an odd-even vehicle rule in Delhi. A newspaper says that most Delhi residents favour the rule. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The poll was conducted in September.
Respondents were interviewed in person.
All the respondents were recruited at Metro stations.
The poll was commissioned by a newspaper.
questions.explanation: Metro users do not drive much, so they are likely to favour the restriction; the sample is biased and does not represent the residents.
questions.shortcut: Look for a biased sample behind a generalisation.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A cement company says its new brand is the strongest because eight out of ten engineers it surveyed preferred it. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The survey was done by telephone.
Cement is sold in 50 kg bags.
All ten engineers surveyed were employees of the company.
The brand was launched last year.
questions.explanation: Employees of the company are not independent judges, so the survey gives biased support.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A school says that chess-club members have high mathematics scores, and concludes that playing chess improves mathematics. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The chess club has 40 members.
Chess tournaments are held twice a year.
Children are admitted to the chess club only after they clear a school-wide mathematics aptitude test.
Mathematics classes are held in the morning.
questions.explanation: If selection into the club depends on mathematical ability, the high scores come first and are not caused by chess.

questions.questionText: Read the following: The metro rail corporation says that its off-peak discount raised off-peak ridership by 18%, and therefore reduced peak-hour crowding. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The discount is 10% on the normal fare.
Off-peak hours are 11 am to 4 pm.
Most of the extra off-peak riders earlier travelled by bus at off-peak times, and peak-hour ridership did not change.
The metro has smart-card readers at all stations.
questions.explanation: Peak crowding falls only if peak riders shift; if the new off-peak riders were never peak riders, peak crowding stays unchanged.

questions.questionText: Read the following: A biscuit maker claims its sugar-free biscuits are healthier than its regular ones. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Sugar-free biscuits are sold in green packs.
Regular biscuits have been sold for 40 years.
To compensate for the sugar, the sugar-free biscuits contain more refined flour and fat and have more calories than regular ones.
Some customers prefer sweet biscuits.
questions.explanation: Removing sugar does not make a product healthier if it is replaced by other less healthy ingredients; the extra calories weaken the claim.

questions.questionText: Read the following: After a highway link to a temple town was built, the average household income in the town rose by 20%. A planner says the tourism the highway brought raised incomes. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The highway is 80 km long.
Temples are open from 5 am to 9 pm.
The whole rise came from a large factory opened in the town in the same year, whose employees are all residents.
The town's population is about 40,000.
questions.explanation: If the income gain is fully explained by the factory, tourism is not needed to explain it.

questions.questionText: Read the following: Researchers found that Indian cities with more tree cover have lower summer temperatures. They conclude that planting more trees in a city will lower its summer temperature. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Tree planting drives are held in July.
Trees give shade.
Cities with more tree cover are mostly located on the coast or in hills, where summers are cooler regardless of trees.
The temperatures were recorded by weather stations.
questions.explanation: Geography is a common cause of both tree cover and cooler weather, so the correlation does not show that planting trees would cool a city.
